answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Binding. Each identity must answer a random challenge derived from its own registration history; clones sharing history give identical answers, so the system flags them. A fresh identity instead needs a unique challenge path, forcing attackers to acquire separate histories. One vault stores each identity's challenge seed; a tundra of cold keys makes reuse detectable. A periodic pulse check re-samples histories, costing an attacker one full independent registration and hosting cycle per clone kept live.
